solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ancient Greek bronze on pole

indicators.note: on says the bronze piece is placed after the pole piece in this across answer

parts.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship's rigging
tan is a bronze colour, as of suntanned skin

explanation.surface: A bronze statue of an ancient Greek stands mounted on a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the colour after the pole in the across reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Sparta, the militarily famous city-state, was an ancient Greek.

clue.text: Not all set up for an iMessaging class

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone organises a lesson conducted through phone messages, but not everyone is set up for it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' means read upwards, so the hidden run RANIMES is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small teaching group or session at a university.

clue.text: Ancient sea tool primarily getting sailor in position

definitions.text: Ancient sea tool primarily getting sailor in position

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of the three words before it
in says the sailor sits inside the word for position

parts.note: a role is a position or post
AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: An old navigational instrument whose use gives a sailor his position at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the astrolabe fixed a sailor's position.
explanation.definitionFit: The astrolabe was an early instrument sailors used to measure the altitude of stars and so fix latitude.

clue.text: Roughly time to cover trunk

indicators.note: in a down clue the T sits on top of the other piece, covering it

parts.note: 'or so' means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: It takes about this long to put a cover on a trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Roughly gives OR SO; T goes above it in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Wife with new bow for male flower

indicators.note: for says the new pieces stand in place of the male letter

parts.note: missus is informal for a wife
an arc is a bow, a curve

explanation.surface: A husband swaps his wife for a new beau, with a flower as token.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests a beau; it is ARC. N and ARC replace the M of MISSUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus is the genus of daffodils and jonquils, a spring bulb plant.

clue.text: Last of malt spirit with favourite bit of 4

indicators.note: Last of says take only the final letter of malt

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A barfly finishes the malt, has a rum and a favourite drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is NARCISSUS: the trumpet is the central cup of a daffodil flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpet is the long tubular corona at the centre of a daffodil bloom.

clue.text: Child and setter lifted Apache symbol?

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the setter's word is read upwards

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as ME

explanation.surface: A child and the crossword setter hold up an Apache emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'lifted' turns only the setter's word upwards; the child stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblematic object or animal; the question mark admits it is a loose example for an Apache tribe.

clue.text: Emir found prancing in regalia

indicators.note: prancing means moving about friskily, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An emir is discovered strutting about in ceremonial dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uniformed is dressed in official or ceremonial attire, like regalia.

clue.text: Turn container to catch drip

indicators.note: to catch says the pot holds the drip inside it

parts.note: a pot is a container
IV, intravenous, is the hospital drip

explanation.surface: Someone turns a pot round to catch a dripping leak.
explanation.walkthrough: The drip here is the hospital kind, fed into a vein, not a leaking tap.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to turn on a central point or axis.

clue.text: Row from Crete possibly with artist aboard

indicators.note: aboard says the artist gets on inside the other letters
possibly says the island's letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone sets out from Crete, perhaps with a painter on the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: TERCE, from Crete rearranged, takes RA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, in British usage.

clue.text: It can be read just over yard in Maine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gauge such as a gas ..., which is read
second meaning: the American spelling of metre, a little over a yard

explanation.surface: Something legible in Maine stands just beyond a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: Maine stands for the US, where metre is spelt this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter is a measuring device whose dial is read, and also US spelling for the 39-inch unit.

clue.text: Game collector on voyage losing power always

parts.note: re means on or about

indicators.note: losing says the power letter is dropped from the trip

parts.note: a trip is a voyage
ever means always

explanation.surface: A sailor on a voyage forever losing his strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' here means shot birds, not a sport, and 'on' is the 're' of business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a gun dog bred to fetch shot birds for the hunter.

clue.text: Recent coinage record splits monies incorrectly

indicators.note: splits says the record goes into the middle of the other letters
incorrectly says the letters of monies are wrongly ordered

parts.note: a log is a record

explanation.surface: A newly minted coin is logged while money is miscounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coinage' points at money, which 'monies' reinforces, but the definition means a coined word.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly invented word or expression, a fresh coinage of language.

clue.text: It's back in centre of Goan port Cato used?

indicators.note: in says the reversed letters go inside
centre of says take the two middle letters of Goan
back says those letters are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as the letters ITS

explanation.surface: A traveller in Goa wonders about a harbour used by the Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato was a statesman of ancient Rome, so 'port Cato used' points to a Roman harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient harbour town of Rome, so a Roman like Cato would have used it.

clue.text: Paddle right ahead before children fish

indicators.note: ahead says the right letter moves to the front of the word

parts.note: an oar is a paddle

explanation.surface: Children paddle ahead to the right and then go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddle' looks like a verb about wading; it is the noun for a rowing blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Writer put on lady's clothing in a weary way

indicators.note: put on says the writer comes first with the clothing letters placed after him

parts.note: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines

indicators.note: clothing says take just the outer letters of the lady word, its covering

parts.note: the word lady, whose outside letters are used

explanation.surface: A male author dons a woman's outfit and looks exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside of LADY, its 'clothing', gives L and Y, which follow HAGGARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggardly describes acting in a gaunt, worn-out manner, like someone exhausted.

clue.text: Extremely stoic search for packs of Players

indicators.note: Extremely says take the two end letters of stoic

parts.note: to rummage is to search

explanation.surface: A calm person hunts through packets of Player's cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: Player's was a cigarette brand, but here the packs are rugby forwards. A rugby scrummage is where the two packs bind together.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a scrummage is the set piece in which each team's forwards push against the other pack.

clue.text: Missing one in the saddle, as is the writer in 14

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a horse with no rider
second meaning: H. Rider Haggard without his Rider is Haggard, the writer in 14

explanation.walkthrough: The writer in 14 is Haggard, whose full name is H. Rider Haggard, so the 14 entry shows him with 'Rider' less.
explanation.definitionFit: Riderless describes a horse with nobody mounted on it, like one that has thrown its jockey.

clue.text: A Mass in church on what may be split seating

indicators.note: in says the mass letter goes inside the church letters

parts.note: RC is the Roman Catholic church
people split hairs when they quibble

explanation.surface: Mass is said in church, with the congregation sitting on divided seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service, but is just its abbreviation; 'what may be split' comes from the idiom about quibbling over trivia.
explanation.definitionFit: Armchairs are comfortable chairs with side arms, a kind of seating.

clue.text: Enthused class interrupting planner briefly in turn

indicators.note: in turn says the whole is then read backwards
interrupting says the class goes into the middle of the other letters
briefly says the last letter of the planner word is cut

parts.note: a designer is a planner
RE, religious education, is a school class

explanation.surface: A lesson cuts short a planner, who becomes excited in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: DESIGNE (designer cut short) takes RE inside to make DESIGRENE, which is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To be energised is to be filled with vigour and enthusiasm.

clue.text: Old bed accommodating one's deed

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: accommodating says the plot holds the one inside it

parts.note: a plot is a garden bed
I is one, as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An old bed with room for one person becomes a heroic act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' sounds like furniture; it is a garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or daring feat, a notable act.

clue.text: Some scared emu ravages object

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A frightened emu wreaks havoc on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' is the verb here, not a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance.

clue.text: Recruits felt exposed with something deadly below

indicators.note: in a down clue the sin sits underneath
exposed says the outer letters are stripped off

parts.note: groped means felt about with the hands
a sin, as one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: New soldiers feel vulnerable with a lethal danger lurking beneath them.
explanation.walkthrough: GROPED stripped of its ends gives ROPE, with SIN below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rope in is to persuade or enlist someone to take part.

clue.text: Sections of Spanish dishes swapped for shells?

indicators.note: Sections of says the dish word is treated as two parts
swapped says those two parts change places

parts.note: tapas are Spanish snack dishes

explanation.surface: Parts of a Spanish meal are exchanged for seafood shells.
explanation.walkthrough: TA and PAS swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Shells, conchiglie, are one shape of the Italian staple; the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Hawk encircles hot exterior

indicators.note: encircles says the selling word goes round the hot letter

parts.note: to hawk is to sell goods, as a pedlar
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A bird of prey circles around a sweltering outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird; it is the verb to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell is a hard outer casing or framework.

clue.text: Fabulous vessel's obstructing Nick's vessel

indicators.note: obstructing says the legendary ship's letters block the middle of the other word

parts.note: a chip is a nick, a small notch
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek legend; with the 's gives ARGOS

explanation.surface: A legendary ship gets in the way of a boat belonging to someone called Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from fable: the Argo of Jason and the Argonauts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cargo ship is a freight-carrying merchant vessel.

clue.text: Tin and heavier metal both ultimately lost capital

indicators.note: both ultimately lost says each word drops its final letter

parts.note: a can is a tin
iron is a metal heavier than tin

explanation.surface: Tin and a denser metal were both lost in the end, costing money.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN and IRON each lose their last letter, giving CA and IRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Start to overplay career in US airport

indicators.note: Start to says take the first letter of overplay

parts.note: to career is to rush along, as is to hare

explanation.surface: An actor begins hamming it up on a career in an American terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is the verb, to go headlong, which is also to hare.
explanation.definitionFit: O'Hare is the international airport serving Chicago.

clue.text: Finished road in a state of high activity

parts.note: over means finished
a drive is a road

explanation.surface: A road is done, and things are hectic.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in overdrive is to be working at an intensely busy, frenetic pitch.

clue.text: Sign Harry is periodically taking drugs

indicators.note: periodically says take every other letter, starting with the second

parts.note: Es are ecstasy tablets

explanation.surface: An astrologer notes that Harry occasionally takes drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of HARRY IS give ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Cry from Hunt when account comes before House

indicators.note: comes before puts the account first

parts.note: a tally is a running account or score

explanation.surface: Someone named Hunt shouts when an account is presented before the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunt with a capital looks like a politician's name; it is a fox hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the cry of huntsmen on sighting a fox.

clue.text: Coating of soft stone damaged plain tile?

indicators.note: Coating of says take the outside letters of soft
damaged says the letters of stone are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plain roof tile, glazed over a soft damaged stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is slang for a hat, and 'plain' points to the American Great Plains, so a cowboy's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is the broad-brimmed cowboy hat worn on the prairies; tile is old slang for headgear.
